method: Reproduced both reviewers' findings against the binding model and checker, including the closed-schema escapes and V10's direct contradiction.
Separated cloud/CI upload, backup custody, and permission exposure instead of retaining an unsupported prevalence claim.
Designed per-project deletion and hostile-output projection protocols, then cross-joined all eighteen properties to live operability gates.
Kept V10 unresolved: repairing contradictory prose is not evidence that the retention/evaluation-proof architecture has been selected.
Added eleven checker mutations covering schema deletion, false publication, V10 greenwashing, deletion, detector, secret-scope, cleanup, and output-safety defects.

findingDispositions.evidence: V5/R5 made real deletion absolute while content-addressed cross-project sharing, crash recovery, and verification were unspecified.
findingDispositions.reasoning: Real deletion is architecture, but it can be made implementable by removing cross-project physical sharing and defining ownership/tombstone/recovery semantics; external OS copies remain outside the promise.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Select ProjectId-namespaced ownership, forbid cross-project deduplication, define within-project references, crash-safe purge and post-purge verification, and narrow the protection domain.
findingDispositions.verification: T7 validates deletionProtocol and rejects cross-project sharing/protocol deletion. R5 remains undemonstrated in operability.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A cryptographic-erasure design with an equally explicit ownership and verification proof could replace this mechanism.

findingDispositions.evidence: No real-client corpus supports exhaustive sync detection and V2's prevalence wording was asserted.
findingDispositions.reasoning: The architecture needs a closed detector result and safe normative fallback now; real-client prevalence/coverage is a pre-release qualification gap, not an invitation to guess.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Version detector catalogs, return DETECTED/NOT-DETECTED/UNKNOWN, refuse or disclose by class, and require G13 qualification on real clients.
findingDispositions.verification: T8 checks detector classes/outcomes and V2/V17/V18 split; publication remains blocked until demonstration.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A maintained cross-platform corpus could improve confidence and admission policy but would not make detection exhaustive.

findingDispositions.evidence: The former gate wording could be read as requiring observed field incidents before qualification.
findingDispositions.reasoning: Controlled adversarial CI can qualify a harness; a release claim still needs release-bound demonstration.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: State the pre-production qualification path and retain the QUALIFIED versus DEMONSTRATED distinction.
findingDispositions.verification: shipGate.qualification and operability gateQualification encode this rule; T4 derives publication only from DEMONSTRATED gates.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Nothing material; field incidents can add controls but are not a prerequisite for initial qualification.

findingDispositions.evidence: The original model and its cross-checked contracts shared an author.
findingDispositions.reasoning: Two independent final reviews diversify the defect search, but coordinator adjudication and future specialist threat review remain valuable process controls.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Register both reviews and do not use checker agreement as sole seal evidence.
findingDispositions.verification: Both review artifacts are registered; completeness consumes their finding IDs and this adjudication.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A security-specialist review may discover new model gaps and should reopen the affected properties.

findingDispositions.evidence: Finding severities and required-property gate values violated their own schemas; schema removal and arbitrary enum replacements escaped.
findingDispositions.reasoning: A closed model is binding only if instances are validated against it and gate identities join to the live operability contract.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Normalize severities, replace gate categories with exact gateIds/expectedSubject, and validate all closed schemas.
findingDispositions.verification: T3/T4 reject enum, schema, missing-gate, stale-gate, and wrong-subject mutations.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: An equivalent generated schema validator with the same live joins.

findingDispositions.evidence: V10 simultaneously claimed resolution and admitted it remained unresolved; the candidate proof did not establish universal predicate outcomes.
findingDispositions.reasoning: This is the highest-risk paper seal. The only honest repair available on this surface is retraction and an explicit architecture blocker.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Mark V10 UNRESOLVED throughout, demote tier/proof sketches to non-authoritative history, and require an independently checked evaluation proof plus selected retention custody before resolution.
findingDispositions.verification: T6 rejects any resolved/both-hold/default language and requires UNRESOLVED-CONTRADICTION. V10 remains a claim-register seal blocker.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A selected retention disposition and independently verified exact-activation/outcome/closure proof covering relational, no-match, degradation, and purge semantics.

findingDispositions.evidence: Cloud sync, backup custody, and world-readable permissions were conflated and described with unsupported prevalence language.
findingDispositions.reasoning: They have different detectors, consequences, confidence, and admission responses.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Split V2, V17, and V18; remove prevalence claims; define detector results, overrides, and platform qualification.
findingDispositions.verification: T8 validates all three classes and rejects conflation/prevalence mutations.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Measured prevalence may support product guidance, not recombining the threat classes.

findingDispositions.evidence: Required properties named categories rather than gates, current state was authored prose, and the checker did not read operability.
findingDispositions.reasoning: Privacy/offline publication must be a derived cross-artifact decision, not self-attestation.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Map every property to exact live gate IDs and product subject; derive a closed publication decision from DEMONSTRATED release evidence.
findingDispositions.verification: T4 loads operability.v2, validates all 18 mappings, and derives BLOCKED with 18 undemonstrated properties; false-green mutations fail.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: An equivalent authoritative release-evidence index mechanically joined to these gates.

findingDispositions.evidence: R5 had no ownership, sharing, tombstone, compaction/recovery, shared-object, or verification protocol.
findingDispositions.reasoning: The deletion claim must name exactly which bytes the tool owns and how crash-safe removal is established.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Add the per-project deletion protocol and disclose external-copy limits.
findingDispositions.verification: T7 mutation-controls sharing, protocol states, and verification; G5 remains IMPLEMENTABLE rather than demonstrated.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A stronger deletion mechanism with the same bounded protection-domain honesty.

findingDispositions.evidence: R11's absolute secret promise exceeded its resolved-configuration handle rationale and ignored source/scanner payloads.
findingDispositions.reasoning: Configuration secrets and analyzed hostile text are different input classes and require different projection policies.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Scope R11 to resolved-config secret values; add R16 class-based source/scanner controls with no default raw excerpts and bounded explicit materialization.
findingDispositions.verification: T9 rejects an arbitrary-source secret absolute; T11 enforces projection class handling.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A proven complete detector for all secret/PII forms; the architecture intentionally makes no such claim.

findingDispositions.evidence: Repository-controlled names/snippets/diagnostics reached terminal, HTML, structured, and agent outputs without a threat property or gate.
findingDispositions.reasoning: Output is an active boundary: ANSI/OSC, HTML/script, URI/path, Unicode, and oversized payloads can harm users and downstream clients.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Add V19/R16, context-specific escaping/neutralization, strict offline CSP/no contribution code, typed machine fields, safe paths/URIs, and adversarial cross-surface fixtures.
findingDispositions.verification: T11 validates five fixture classes and all projection contexts; output-safety deletion/weakening mutations fail.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A surface-independent safe-value type could replace per-surface controls only if it proves the same contextual guarantees.

findingDispositions.evidence: Guaranteed cleanup on every exit was impossible under SIGKILL, power loss, and host crash.
findingDispositions.reasoning: The enforceable absolute is no shared temp; private ownership, inventory, bounded retention, and startup scavenging handle crash residue honestly.
findingDispositions.requiredChange: Replace instantaneous cleanup guarantee with restrictive creation, owned inventory, recovery scavenging, and purge visibility.
findingDispositions.verification: T10 rejects all-exit cleanup claims and requires the crash-resilient controls while preserving the shared-temp prohibition.
findingDispositions.whatWouldChangeMyMind: An OS primitive providing durable atomic ephemeral storage across all supported platforms; none is assumed.

sealedPropertiesCovered: closed threat finding/property schemas and exact operability joins
per-project deletion inside the tool-controlled protection domain
separate sync/upload, backup, and permission-exposure threats
resolved-config secret handling separated from source/scanner text
knownLimitations: V10 remains an unresolved architecture contradiction; no durable-authoritative retention default is selected.
No threat property is DEMONSTRATED, so privacy/offline publication remains BLOCKED.
Storage detectors cannot be exhaustive and require real-client/platform qualification.
Deletion cannot cover OS backups, dumps, swap, indexers, or user-created copies outside the tool's protection domain.

undischargedPropertyClassification.V10 evaluation-proof/retention custody: unresolved architecture decision; durable-authoritative Runs requiring that choice must be excluded until resolved
undischargedPropertyClassification.R1-R18 product properties: legitimate pre-implementation evidence gaps after mechanisms are specified, except V10-dependent retention
undischargedPropertyClassification.storage detector coverage: acceptable measurement question with DETECTED/NOT-DETECTED/UNKNOWN and fail-visible normative fallback
undischargedPropertyClassification.capability-dependent execution: feature that must be excluded until ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT exists

sealRecommendation.note: Reviewer defects are repaired and guarded, but V10 is a load-bearing unresolved architecture choice. A green checker proves the model says OPEN consistently; it does not resolve the choice.
sealRecommendation.consumerB: No for durable-authoritative retention/evaluation proof. Yes only for the bounded deletion, storage-detection, projection-safety, and gate-mapping subcontracts.
